data.description:
The persistence layer for the whole product: schema/migrations plus a repository layer with tests. Entities: freelancer (user), connected Stripe account (id plus readiness flags), client, contract, invoice mirror (our copy of Stripe invoice state), and a processed-webhook-event table for idempotency. No Stripe calls at all — this task is pure persistence and runs in parallel with the custody-guard task.

IMPLEMENTS: docs/engineering/00-d1-v1-milestone-plan.md section 3 rows C-04 (persistence and data model) and C-15 (client records). Both IN under Rule 1.

DECISION CONTEXT. Client records are IN because links 3 and 4 of the v1 chain (a contract FOR a client; an invoice ON that client) require a stored counterparty. A dedicated Clients SCREEN is OUT (row C-16, Rule 1) — clients are created inline from the invoice and contract forms — so this task owns client persistence and no screen owns client management. The Stripe customer (cus_) is created LAZILY at first invoice by the invoice task, not here, so a client the freelancer never invoices leaves no trace on their Stripe account. The connected-account readiness flags (charges_enabled, outstanding requirements) are DEFINED here and MAINTAINED by the Connect task; the invoice task reads them to gate finalize. That three-way contract is why none of those tasks needs an edge to the others beyond this one.

Multi-currency, VAT, and jurisdictional invoice fields are out of v1 (row C-32, Rule 1) but the schema must not foreclose them: a currency column with a single allowed value is fine, a currency hardcoded into every query is not.

VERIFICATION: migrations run from empty on docker compose up; repository tests cover create/read/update plus the uniqueness and foreign-key constraints; the suite runs with no accounts and no network.

NOT IN THIS TASK: authentication or credential handling (the auth task — this task defines the user row, not the credential flow); any Stripe API call; any UI.
data.title: D1 v1: data model and persistence layer (freelancer, connected account, client, contract, invoice mirror)

data.note: persistence lives in the scaffolded app; no Stripe, so no guard edge needed

data.body: Pulled as spine task 4: AS-37 is done and every remaining server task (AS-40/41/42/43) sits behind this one — with AS-38 merged it is the sole gate on the rest of the spine. Owen plans as tech lead; Marcus implements.

Plan written (10 sections, 25 ACs, 18 falsification recipes). Decisions: engine/driver = SQLite via node:sqlite DatabaseSync imported in exactly lib/db/connection.js (WAL, foreign_keys ON, busy_timeout 5000; zero new deps); migrations = ordered JS modules (lib/db/migrations/NNNN-name.js exporting {version,name,up}) run at boot by lib/db/migrate.js inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE against a schema_migrations ledger, refusing a newer DB or a renamed migration, never mkdir; money = integer minor units + per-invoice currency column whose allowed set lives only in lib/db/money.js (DDL checks shape only, so adding a currency is one array entry, not a table rebuild); time = ISO-8601 UTC text as apps/chat does; state machine = STATUS_RANK {draft 0, open 1, uncollectible 2, paid 3, void 3} defined in lib/db/repositories/invoices.js with applyStripeSnapshot -> applied|fields|stale|conflict (paid-before-finalized converges), AS-43 attaches/finalizes, AS-44 applies webhook snapshots + readiness, readiness 'ready' = chargesEnabled && no requirements due, derived in one mapper. Data on named volume invoicing-data at /app/data (Dockerfile chowns it; test service mountless). Guard: node:sqlite sanctioned in 1 file, money words in 4, new raw-SQL concept row allowing 9 lib/db files, source list 14->26, test files 8->10. Size ~26 files/~1,750 lines (over tripwires, justified §7 with a pre-agreed split line); complexity stays medium.

Starting implementation in .worktrees/AS-39 on feat/AS-39-persistence, per the plan (node:sqlite in lib/db/connection.js only; migration 0001 with all eight tables; seven-key repository surface; STATUS_RANK state machine). Baseline suite first, then the §6 recipes with backups outside the repo.

AS-39 implementation report (developer-marcus)

BRANCH / COMMITS. `feat/AS-39-persistence` in `.worktrees/AS-39`, three commits on top of the plan commit 0252e75, each green on the Docker `test` service before it landed, all as developer-marcus <developer-marcus@agents.american-software.local>:
- 68d51b6 AS-39: add the persistence core — connection, migrations, schema DDL, boot wiring and the database health check
- a5d2133 AS-39: add the six repositories, money.js and createRepositories
- 8057a50 AS-39: document the persistence layer in the app README
Worktree clean (`git status --porcelain` empty). `git diff master...feat/AS-39-persistence -- .lattice` is empty; no file outside apps/invoicing/ is touched.

DIFF. `git -C .worktrees/AS-39 diff --stat master...feat/AS-39-persistence | tail -1` -> `26 files changed, 3104 insertions(+), 57 deletions(-)` = 3,161 diff lines. THIS CROSSES THE §7 SPLIT LINE (~2,400). I did not split unilaterally — the orchestrator decides on AS-39b (contracts + invoices repositories, the state machine, the I/K/X tests). Where the §7 estimate missed: lib/db source is 1,418 lines vs ~900 (per-key validation before every SQL statement is ~40% of each repository); tests ~1,600 vs ~650 (db.test.js 461 for D1–D18, repositories.test.js 938 for 59 tests — every §2.10 row got its own test). File count 26 matches §7 exactly.
Files (26): NEW lib/db/connection.js, lib/db/errors.js, lib/db/migrate.js, lib/db/migrations/0001-initial.js, lib/db/database.js, lib/db/money.js, lib/db/repositories/{freelancers,connected-accounts,clients,contracts,invoices,stripe-events}.js, test/db.test.js, test/repositories.test.js. EDITED lib/config.js, lib/health.js, server.js, compose.yaml, Dockerfile, README.md, test/helpers/server.js, test/config.test.js, test/health.test.js, test/harness.test.js, test/deploy-shape.test.js, test/dependency-policy.test.js.

SUITE (offline `test` service, network_mode none, isolated project asc-invoicing-as39): `# tests 195 / # pass 183 / # fail 0 / # skipped 12` (136 pre-existing + 59 repository tests; the 12 skips are the stripe-mock contract tests without the mock). Exactly 10 test files, pinned by harness V2: assets, config, db, dependency-policy, deploy-shape, harness, health, repositories, stripe-client, stripe-mock. `contract` service (stripe-mock v0.203.0 on the internal network): EXIT=0, `# tests 195 / # pass 195 / # fail 0 / # skipped 0`, same 10 files. V1 control `run --rm -e ASC_SELFTEST_MUTATE=1 test`: EXIT=1, exactly `not ok 79 - V1` red (182 pass / 1 fail).

MUTATION QUADRUPLES (§6). Baseline first (183/0). Each row: backup outside the repo -> mutate -> assert applied (grep count printed) -> `run --build` -> record `not ok` set -> restore via EXIT trap -> `git -C $WT diff --exit-code -- apps/invoicing` printed RESTORED-CLEAN for every row -> the next `--build` rebuilds. Final rebuild + run on the restored tree: 183/0. Per-row TAP logs are in the session scratchpad (as39-bak/run-<row>.log), outside the repo.
- M1 | grep -c 'from "node:sqlite"' routes/pages.js => 1 (predicted 1) | not ok #59 dependency-policy "the Stripe concepts live exactly where AS-38 and AS-39 put them…" (the test that carries the node:sqlite scanConcept) | MATCHED, exactly 1
- M2 | foreign_keys = OFF => 1 | D1, D8, A4, C8, X4, X5, X9 (7) | WIDER by D8 (plan: D1+A4+C8+X4+X5+X9). D8 provokes a genuine 787 through the real schema, which needs enforcement on. Predicted by me before the run.
- M3 | REFERENCES clients (id) => 2 | X4, X5 | MATCHED
- M4 | 'bogus' => 1 | X1 | MATCHED
- M5 | void: 4 => 1 | I15 | MATCHED
- M6 | if (false) return outcome => 1 | I13, I14 | MATCHED
- M7 | CREATE INDEX freelancers_email_unique => 1 | D8, F4, F5 | WIDER by D8 (AC 11 says "and nothing else"). D8's 2067 case provokes a real UNIQUE violation through the email index. Predicted by me before the run.
- M8 | assertEditableDraft(row) count 2 -> 1; '^  void row;' => 1 | I9, I11 | MATCHED
- M9 | if (false) continue; => 1 | D4, D15, D18 | MATCHED CLASS (plan: D4, D15 + every test that migrates twice — record the set): the extra is D18, which boots the default path on an already-migrated file.
- M10 | 'eur' => 1 | I2, I3 | MATCHED
- M11 | invoicing-data:/app/data => 0 | deploy-shape #67 (web publishes 8348 + mounts exactly the data volume), #68 (no service bind-mounts — it pins the complete volume list to exactly [['web','invoicing-data:/app/data']]), #69 (image/mount/config agree) | WIDER by #68, a deliberate over-pin in my deploy-shape test
- M12 | chown node:node /app/data => 0 | D18, deploy-shape #69 | MATCHED (two witnesses, as predicted)
- M13 | name: 'database' => 0 | D16, D17, D18, health "there are exactly four checks, by name", health "GET /healthz returns 200 … all four checks passing" | MATCHED CLASS; D18 also pins the four-check healthz
- M14 | '^  void dbPath;' => 1 | D10, D17 | WIDER by D17: with statSync gone the probe's open CREATES an empty file and reports a schema-version mismatch instead of ENOENT; D17 pins /ENOENT/ in the detail. Good for the guard, not the plan's literal set.
- M15 | SELECT 1 FROM freelancers => 1 | #59 dependency-policy (raw SQL concept) | MATCHED, exactly 1
- P1 | invoicing-data:/app/data => 2 | deploy-shape #66 (test service network-blocked and mountless), #68 | WIDER by #68 (same full-list pin as M11)
- P2 | amount => 1 in lib/db/errors.js | #59 dependency-policy (money RAW concept) | MATCHED, exactly 1
- V1 | tree clean | EXIT=1, only V1 red | MATCHED
Procedure finding (mine, fixed): my first V1 run followed P2 without `--build`, ran against the stale P2 image, and showed dependency-policy #59 red next to V1 — the "restored tree, stale mutant image" phantom CLAUDE.md warns about. Rebuilt (the `final` run) and re-ran V1: V1 alone. The §6 V1 recipe as written has no `--build`; run it only after a rebuild.

AC 3–4 / 19 / 5 TRANSCRIPT (isolated project asc-invoicing-as39). The live asc-invoicing-web-1 owns 127.0.0.1:8348, so the host port was remapped to 127.0.0.1:18348 by an override file OUTSIDE the repo (`ports: !override`); merged config verified — container port 8348, the invoicing-data volume and the build context unchanged. asc-invoicing-web-1 and asc-chat-server-1 were never touched and were still Up (healthy) afterwards.
- from nothing (`down -v`, no invoicing volumes): `up --build -d web` -> healthy in 7 s; logs: `database /app/data/invoicing.sqlite: schema v1, applied 1 migration(s)` then `invoicing listening on 0.0.0.0:8348 {"port":8348,…,"dbPath":"/app/data/invoicing.sqlite","stripeSecretKey":null}`; GET /healthz -> HTTP 200, ok:true, 4 checks config/vendor_assets/views/database all true; `docker volume ls` -> asc-invoicing-as39_invoicing-data (under the default project name the same rule yields asc-invoicing_invoicing-data; the live web-1 predates this branch and has no volume).
- `restart web` -> `applied 0 migration(s)`.
- AC 19: `time docker compose stop web` -> real 0.263 s; container exit code 0.
- `down` (volume kept) -> `up -d web` -> `applied 0 migration(s)`.
- `down -v` (volume removed) -> `up -d web` -> `applied 1 migration(s)`. Final `down -v`.
- AC 5: `run --rm -e INVOICING_DB_PATH=/nonexistent/x.sqlite --no-deps web` -> EXIT=1, `Error: cannot open database /nonexistent/x.sqlite: unable to open database file` (prepareDatabase, lib/db/database.js:54). Repeated inside ONE container followed by a check: boot EXIT=1, path named in the output, /nonexistent NOT-CREATED.
Cleanup: all as39 containers, networks and volumes removed (needed `--profile '*' down -v --remove-orphans` — a plain `down` leaves the contract run's profile-gated stripe-mock container up); images asc-invoicing-as39-{web,test,contract} removed; stripe/stripe-mock:v0.203.0 and the live project's images kept. No global prune.

DEPENDENCY-POLICY ALLOWLISTS (test/dependency-policy.test.js): source list 19 -> 26 (lib/db/connection.js, errors.js, migrate.js, migrations/0001-initial.js, database.js, money.js, repositories/{clients,connected-accounts,contracts,freelancers,invoices,stripe-events}.js — the first five landed in commit 1, the rest in commit 2); raw SQL allowlist -> exactly 9 files (connection.js, migrate.js, migrations/0001-initial.js + the six repositories); money RAW allowlist (comments count) -> exactly four: lib/db/migrations/0001-initial.js, lib/db/money.js, lib/db/repositories/invoices.js, lib/stripe/custody.js (a grep over lib/, routes/, server.js agrees); node:sqlite import allowlist unchanged ['lib/db/connection.js'] — the other node:sqlite mentions in lib/db are JSDoc `import('node:sqlite')` types and comments, and M1 shows the scan ignores them. Harness literal 9 -> 10.
Other AC greps: `requirementsCurrentlyDue.length` exactly 1 hit (connected-accounts.js); 'usd' in lib/db only in money.js; longest file repositories.test.js 938 lines (< 1,200); schema = 8 tables (7 entity + schema_migrations), 4 named indexes + 13 autoindexes, all STRICT.

DEVIATIONS (numbered):
1. §2.7 probe order: `statSync(dbPath)` runs FIRST, before the directory W_OK check and the open, so a missing file reports ENOENT and the probe never creates the file. In the plan's order M14 would have been vacuous.
2. AC 9 / D3 say "5 indexes"; the DDL has 4 named indexes (freelancers_email_unique, clients_owner_email, contracts_owner_created, invoices_owner_created). D3 pins 4 named + 13 autoindexes. Nothing was dropped — the plan's count is off by one.
3. §2.8: the engine's CANTOPEN message ("unable to open database file") carries no path, so prepareDatabase wraps it as `cannot open database <path>: <cause>` with `{ cause }` kept — AC 5 needs the path in the failure.
4. Three commits, not the suggested four: the "boot wiring + health" slice cannot be green alone (server.js needs prepareDatabase; deploy-shape needs the compose/Dockerfile changes), so it landed with the core. AS-38 precedent.
5. §6 scaffold: Node 24 prints the spec reporter even off-TTY, so run_suite passes `node --test --test-reporter=tap` as the compose command override (the test service command itself stays bare `node --test`; its guard is untouched) and adds -T; BAK is the session scratchpad rather than `mktemp -d /tmp/…` (still outside the repo). V1 needs a rebuild before it (finding above).
6. §2.10 lists X as 8 rows, but the composite-FK row is "invoices AND contracts" and M3's predicted set names two tests — X is 9 tests (X4 invoices, X5 contracts): 59 repository tests, 195 total.
7. AC 21's "from" literals were stale: master had 9 (harness) and 19 (dependency-policy source list), not 8 and 14. The "to" values 10 / 26 hold.
8. Predicted-set mismatches (all above): M2 and M7 wider by D8; M11 and P1 wider by deploy-shape #68; M14 wider by D17; M9 and M13 wider within the predicted class by D18. Nothing narrower. No test was weakened to make a set match. Options for QA/orchestrator: accept the literal sets as recorded, or move D8's 2067 case onto clients.stripe_customer_id (M7 would then be exactly F4+F5; M2 still carries D8's 787).
9. (not code) compose `down` without --profile leaves a profile-gated stripe-mock up after a contract run — worth a line in the README's contract-run notes later; not done, outside scope.

UNDONE / QA POINTERS. Nothing in §2/§3 is unimplemented. Not done by design: the §9 CLAUDE.md wording (metawork layer). §7 split is the orchestrator's call: 3,161 > ~2,400. QA first looks: (1) lib/db/repositories/invoices.js applySnapshot — STATUS_RANK, the fields/stale/conflict outcomes, and that attachStripeInvoice is the only path that sets stripe_invoice_id on a draft; (2) assertOwnedClient in contracts.js/invoices.js including updateDraft clientId changes; (3) D8 under M2/M7 and D17 under M14 — plan literal vs test; (4) README `down -v` warning and the migration-adding recipe.

Split-line call (plan §7): measured 3,161 lines vs the ~2,400 pre-agreed line. Not splitting post-hoc — file count is exactly the planned 26, the miss is the line estimate (validation code and one-test-per-row), and carving finished, recipe-proven code into AS-39b reviews the same lines twice and delivers nothing sooner. Review proceeds whole, as AS-37 did at 3,113. The plan's second trigger (cycle 2 on scope grounds) stays as the backstop; §7 addendum records it.
